title: Reject plans where multiple steps target the same file without ordering
problem: runner/validate_plan.py does not check for file overlap across steps. If steps 3 and 7 both list runner/foo.py in step.files without a transitive depends_on between them, the topological sort produces a nondeterministic order. The two steps then race — one will silently overwrite the other's edits, and the runner has no signal that anything went wrong.
description:
Add a new helper _check_file_overlap(steps) to runner/validate_plan.py. For every pair of steps (i, j) that share at least one entry in their files lists, verify that either i transitively depends_on j or j transitively depends_on i. If neither, emit an error:

  step[i] and step[j] both target <file> without an ordering   constraint — add depends_on, or merge into one step.

Compute transitive dependencies via DFS over the existing depends_on graph. Skip pairs where one or both steps have action='test' or action='verify' (those don't write files).

Wire into validate() after the cycle check (so we know the graph is acyclic).

Tests:
- two write-action steps sharing a file with no depends_on ->   rejected
- two write-action steps sharing a file with direct depends_on   -> accepted
- two write-action steps sharing a file with transitive   depends_on (via a third step) -> accepted
- two write-action steps with disjoint files -> accepted
- a test step and a write step sharing a file -> accepted   (test steps don't write)
- three steps where 1 and 3 share a file, 1->2->3 chain exists   -> accepted (transitive dependency suffices)
- full validate() surfaces the new error class
context: Filed as scribe TODO #241. Pure additive validation; existing plans that already declare proper depends_on chains are unaffected. Catches a class of race conditions the planner can introduce silently.
